summary: The batch is safe for children apart from one crash-site Epic (light bar), a cliff-jump Rare (action camera) and a headlight-dazzling Rare (reflector), and its Commons and Uncommons are mostly real, recognisable habits (lens cap left on, controller drift, snooze button, the forty hours of dashcam nothing). Above Uncommon it is the weakest batch so far. About 60 of 98 Legendaries use the banned 'has done X for N years / still has its first bulb / never once' formula, about 40 Rares are the object simply doing its job well (lit the path, guided the boat, balanced the sound), and about 40 Epics are crowd scenes ('lit every desk in the library', 'the whole street sang along'). Most lines in those three rarities need rewriting; a replacement and a paired name are given for each. Clusters blur together: the tape objects share Commons and Epics, the light fixtures all 'lit X so warmly that everyone gathered', and six light objects guide someone lost home. Names: 67 Legendaries are 'Old/Grand/Lady X of the Y', six objects have names swapped or rotated between rarities (paper lantern, reflector, jukebox, CD changer, fuse box, fire extinguisher), and there are trademark echoes (Kodachrome, Polaroo, Gamestation, Spinmaster, Daredevil, Bluetooth). Move mechanics are mostly respected (burn names have heat, drain names snatch), but about 30 move names are garbled repeats ('Moth Moth Moth Moth', 'Flash Flash Flash Flash' on a single hit), and a few varying Ultimates promise one effect ('Game Over Daze', 'Neon Glare', 'Heating Surge'). The good lines to keep and imitate are the dashcam, extension cord, doorbell, fire alarm, speaker Epic and Legendary, and the soundbar Rare.

patterns.pattern: Legendary formula 'has done X for N years / still has its first X / never once': the default Legendary in this batch (about 60 of 98). Each is a nice record, not an outrageous feat with a punchline.
patterns.suggestion: Rewrite each as one outrageous feat plus a deflating punchline (replacements are given per object). Never 'for N years', 'still has', 'never once', 'the same family'.

patterns.pattern: Rare = the object doing its job well (lit the path, guided the boat, balanced the sound, filmed beautifully, matched the beat). The lessons require a troublesome POWER.
patterns.suggestion: Give each Rare a power that causes trouble (shows the wrong room, plays everything too fast, swaps the chorus, lights only the vegetable-refuser's plate).

patterns.pattern: Epic crowd formula: 'every X at the Y at once', 'lit every desk/corridor/barn dance', 'the whole street/town/hall cheered or sang along', or a crowd plus a comparison ('like a river of stars', 'a hundred halos').
patterns.suggestion: Replace each with one concrete disruption and a joke (the egg box cracks, the cast performs in the living room, the snowman comes in for a drink).

patterns.pattern: Legendary name monotony: 67 of 98 Legendaries are 'Old X of the Y', 'Grand X of the Y' or 'Lady/Sir/Captain X of the Y'. Several stems repeat (Watchwell x2, Lumina x2).
patterns.suggestion: New Legendary names are given with each rewrite and mix shapes: 'Name, the Epithet', 'Name the Adjective', pun names ('Beatbox Betty', 'Transistor Tess'), and plain titles.

patterns.pattern: Lost-and-guided-home frame repeats across the light objects (beacon boat, lantern lost family, lantern light lost sheep and hiker, candle holder traveller, torch lost dog, flashlight lost cat).
patterns.suggestion: Keep at most one rescue line in the cluster, and make even that one funny.

patterns.pattern: Light-fixture cluster tell-apart: chandelier = crystals and mirrors; chandelier light = candle bulbs and romance; ceiling light = switching on and off; pendant = low and swinging; floor light = tall and looming; desk light = bendy neck; wall lamp = hallway sneaking; reading light = bedtime books; ring light = flattering faces; studio light = heat. Lanterns: lantern = shadows; lantern light = swinging; oil lantern = soot; paper lantern = fragile paper.
patterns.suggestion: Change the light lines that are now near each other (they all 'lit X so warmly that everyone gathered') using the per-object replacements, which follow this split.

patterns.pattern: Tape cluster near-copies: i_cassette C, x_cassette_tape C and x_tape_deck C (tape chewed or spilled); x_cassette_tape E = x_tape_deck E (recording the Sunday chart for the class); three tape Legendaries 'for N years'. Projectors x4 and cameras also share 'did its job beautifully' Rares.
patterns.suggestion: Keep i_cassette C (chewed tape) and change the other two; tell the tape objects apart: cassette = old music and rewinding, cassette tape = recordings and labels, tape deck = copying and clunky buttons.

patterns.pattern: Garbled repeated move names (four or five copies of one word, or a doubled word on a single-hit move): 'Moth Moth Moth Moth', 'Flash Flash Flash Flash', 'Skip Skip Skip Skip Skip', 'Pixel Flash Flash', 'Power Snatch Snatch', 'Mix Boost Boost'.
patterns.suggestion: Use at most three copies of a word, and only on the ×3 moves; single-hit stun, drain and boost moves get one clear image.

patterns.pattern: Brand and trademark echoes in names: Kodachrome, Polaroo (Polaroid), Gamestation (PlayStation), Spinmaster (Spin Master), Daredevil, Bluetooth, Volumeeleven (film catchphrase). The i_ipod / x_ipod_nano labels are brands; their text is correctly generic.
patterns.suggestion: Rename as given per object; keep all text brand-free.

patterns.pattern: Ultimates whose effect varies by variant but whose names promise one effect: 'Game Over Daze', 'Giant Picture Glare', 'Neon Glare', 'Spotlight Glare', 'Heating Surge'; plus Ultimates that repeat the Epic name ('Foam Flood', 'Blackout').
patterns.suggestion: Use effect-neutral finisher images ('Neon Finale', 'Dial Spin Finale') and give each Ultimate its own picture.

patterns.pattern: Many lore lines are under 60 characters with no consequence (about 100 lines; e.g. 'Squeaks every time you bend it.', 'Glows over homework every evening.', 'Made a coffee and forgot the cup.').
patterns.suggestion: Aim for 60 to 160 characters: the habit, then a small concrete punchline.
